model_annotation: This chart is a nested donut (ring) chart consisting of two concentric rings that represent two different metrics related to ambiguity. The outer ring displays categories based on standard deviation (Std) values, divided into four slices: "Std: 0.0" shown in dark navy at approximately 0.0%, "Std: 0.47" in a dark teal-blue at 47.7%, "Std: 0.82" in a medium blue at 38.0% (appearing as the second-largest slice), and "Std: 0.94" in a lighter sky blue comprising the remaining portion. The percentage labels visible on the outer ring include 47.7%, .0%, 7.0%, and 5.0%, though some labels appear to correspond to transitions between the outer and inner rings. The inner ring represents "Max Ambiguity" and is divided into three slices: "Max: 1" in a medium-light blue at 14.2%, "Max: 2" in a lighter cyan-blue at 39.0%, and "Max: 3" in the palest light blue at 38.0%. Two separate legends are provided to the right of the chart — one for the outer ring labeled "(Outer)" and one for the inner ring labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)" — each using color-coded squares to identify the categories. Percentage labels are displayed directly on or near the corresponding slices. The chart title at the top right appears partially obscured or blurred. The largest slice in the outer ring is "Std: 0.47" at 47.7%, while in the inner ring, "Max: 2" and "Max: 3" are nearly equal in size at 39.0% and 38.0%, respectively.
